**Shuttle with the second‑fewest construction‑milestone entries (before 2024) – Challenger (OV‑099)**  
The NASA reference guide lists the following numbers of construction‑milestone items for each orbiter:  
- Challenger: 11 milestones (page excerpt shows 11 dated entries from 1979–1983).  
- Endeavour: 10 milestones (lowest count).  
- Discovery, Atlantis, Columbia: 25, 11 (tie), and 30 milestones, respectively.  
Thus Challenger has the second‑fewest milestones (after Endeavour) among the five completed or b‑uilding shuttles.  

*Sources:* NASA Reference Guide: “The Space Shuttle” – Construction Milestones section, which provides the milestone lists for Challenger, Endeavour, etc. (see excerpts in the fetched page).  

**Challenger missions that landed at the Shuttle Landing Facility (EAFB)**  
The “Flights of Challenger (OV‑099)” table (PDF, 2023) lists all Challenger flights and records the landing site.  Every Challenger flight landed at Edwards AFB (the Shuttle Landing Facility).  The missions are:  

| Mission | Launch date | Landing date (EAFB) | Primary payload |
|---------|------------|----------------------|-----------------|
| STS‑6 | 4 Apr 1983 | 9 Apr 1983 | TDRS‑1 |
| STS‑7 | 18 Jun 1983 | 24 Jun 1983 | Anik C‑2 / Palapa B‑1 |
| STS‑8 | 30 Aug 1983 | 5 Sep 1983 | INSAT 1 B |
| STS‑41‑C | 6 Apr 1984 | 13 Apr 1984 | Long‑Duration Exposure Facility (LDEF) |
| STS‑51‑B | 6 May 1985 | 6 May 1985 | Spacelab‑3 |
| STS‑51‑F | 29 Jul 1985 | 6 Aug 1985 | Spacelab‑2 |
| STS‑61‑A | 30 Oct 1985 | 6 Nov 1985 | Spacelab‑D‑1 |

These seven flights represent all Challenger missions that landed at EAFB.  No other Challenger missions existed, and every flight listed indeed used the Shuttle Landing Facility as the landing site.
